name: Guénolé

attributes.attribute: Breton saint and abbot of Ys
a lost city of the sea

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Guénolé was a Breton saint and the abbot of the city of Ys. Ys was a doomed city, and it held the pagan princess Dahut. Guénolé saved the King Gradlon, the father of Dahut, as the flood took the city. He gave the king a horse to ride to higher ground. Some liken the holy power of Guénolé to an older sea god. His tale carries the mark of the new faith that came into the land.

okr.objective: Tell the fall of the city of Ys and the kindness of the saint.
key_results: Name the saint and the doomed city.
